zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 家庭信心轉弱，前端美債收復部分跌幅

紐約聯準銀行調查顯示，家庭對就業與還款能力更為擔憂，週一短天期美債因而收復部分非農公布後的跌幅。2 年期殖利率扭轉亞洲時段升勢，下跌 2 個基點至 4.15%；長端則繼續承壓，10 年期上升 1 個基點至 4.56%，30 年期上升 2 個基點至 5.03%。

這份調查使升息判斷更複雜，但還不足以推翻它。短期通膨預期下降，求職展望轉差，逾期還款風險上升；然而，中長期實質殖利率仍走高，10 年期損益兩平通膨率反而下滑。投資人願意回吐部分強勁就業帶來的前端升幅，卻尚未降低對較長天期實質報酬的要求。

科技股也在半導體帶領下反彈，高收益債 ETF 小幅上漲。以色列與伊朗再度交火推高油價，為美國通膨公布與 ECB 會議增添變數。德國工廠訂單明顯轉弱，南韓則因半導體帶動的成長與升息預期，使當地債券持續承壓。另一方面，日本退休基金相關帳戶提供了可觀買盤，5 月海外債券淨買進額創下紀錄。

## 家庭調查緩和非農後的升息預期

美債在亞洲時段一度延續週五跌勢，2 年與 5 年期殖利率升幅大於長端。交換市場再次反映 Fed 在 12 月前升息 25 個基點，並給予第二次升息約 16% 的機率。中東再起衝突，也在強勁就業之外增加油價風險。

紐約聯準銀行 5 月家庭調查對需求的描繪卻較為保守。1 年期通膨預期中位數由 3.6% 降至 3.5%，3 年與 5 年期分別維持 3.1% 與 3.0%。受訪者認為失去工作的機率為 15.1%，失業後找到新工作的機率僅 43.7%；無法支付最低應繳債務的機率上升 1.2 個百分點至 12.6%，預期支出增速也放緩。

在週五急遽調整後，這些數據為前端提供一些支撐。實際招聘雖強，家庭態度卻更審慎，對近期通膨的焦慮也略有下降。收盤時，2 年期債券已回升，5 年期殖利率持平於 4.29%；2s10s 擴大 3 個基點至 41 個基點，2s30s 擴大 4 個基點至 88 個基點。

相對累積升幅，當日回落仍小。過去一週，2 年、5 年、10 年與 30 年期殖利率分別上升 10、11、9 與 4 個基點；過去一個月則上升 25、27、18 與 8 個基點。2s5s10s 蝶式利差上升 1 個基點至 −13 個基點，代表 5 年期當日相對兩翼略為落後；2s10s30s 上升 2 個基點至 −6 個基點。

實質殖利率仍繼續攀升。5 年期 TIPS 上升 1 個基點至 1.82%，7 年期上升 2 個基點至 2.01%，10 年期上升 2 個基點至 2.21%；20 年與 30 年期分別上升 2 與 3 個基點，來到 2.57% 與 2.77%。儘管原油上漲，10 年期損益兩平通膨率卻下跌 1 個基點至 2.35%。能源仍限制 Fed 因應景氣轉弱的空間，但當日並未推高長期通膨補償。

現金市場保持平穩。國庫券債券等值殖利率方面，4 週券持平於 3.68%，6 週券下跌 1 個基點至 3.67%，8 週券持平於 3.69%；13、17 與 26 週券分別上升 3、1 與 2 個基點至 3.74%、3.76% 與 3.82%，52 週券則下跌 3 個基點至 3.82%。

已完成的兩場國庫券標售，需求強弱不一。91 天券標售金額為 $890.01 億，最高得標利率 3.640%，投標倍數由 2.69 升至 2.79；間接投標人取得 56.22%，直接投標人 5.87%，交易商 37.90%。$770 億 182 天券則以 3.690% 得標，投標倍數由 2.84 降至 2.75，交易商取得 40.56%。兩場合計 $1,660.01 億，6 月 11 日交割。13 週券投標倍數改善，較長券種則由交易商承接更多，整體表現分歧，但最短端並未出現失序。

## 融資案持續增加，非公開評等受到檢視

公司信用風險的承擔意願隨股市改善。HYG 上漲 0.14%，JNK 上漲 0.07%，對利率較敏感的 LQD 下跌 0.10%，EMB 下跌 0.13%。S&P 500 上漲 0.30%，Nasdaq 100 上漲 1.58%，費城半導體指數大漲 5.61%；VIX 下跌 12.04% 至 18.92，但經過週五重挫，Nasdaq 過去一週報酬仍為負。

融資案源繼續增加。Blackstone 正研究將民間投資基金持分包裝成債券，交易額可能超過 $20 億，成為近期較大型的同類案件之一。Arcmont 與 Ares 則為 Silver Lake 支持的軟體公司 Cegid 主導 €11 億貸款。兩案都尚在規劃或安排階段，最終條件與投資人需求仍待確認。

哥倫比亞大學收盤後發布的研究，對非公開評等債務提出更根本的疑問。在超過 $4 兆的樣本中，這類資產發生信用損失的可能性，約為同評等公開評等債務的兩倍；非公開 BBB 的減損風險，相當於公開評等 BB+ 或 BB。美國壽險業持有約 $4,810 億非公開評等資產，占具評等信用投資組合 12%，2018 年則不到 2%。研究估計，若讓評等與實際表現相符，可能需要增加約 $45 億資本。

研究仍有重要限制：尚未經同儕審查，樣本處於良好信用環境，損失率低於 1%，Morningstar DBRS 也反對其方法與結論。不過，隨著愈來愈大型的融資移往非公開市場，非公開評等如何使用、保險公司應提列多少資本，已成為值得關注的問題。

亞洲科技公司則同時增加潛在股權與債券供給。Moonshot AI 尋求以 $300 億估值籌集最高 $20 億股權資金；紐約時間下午 5 點過後，市場傳出騰訊準備發行約 $30 億雙幣別債券，最快週二定價。股權資金可降低眼前借款需求，但產業擴張仍需大量晶片、電力與資料中心投資。相較於籌資目標，騰訊最終幣別與天期配置、定價及配售，將更具體呈現債市需求。

## 歐洲權衡能源衝擊，南韓債市持續下跌

德國工廠訂單凸顯 ECB 考慮升息時面對的成長弱點。4 月訂單月減 3.8%，大於預期的 1.2% 降幅，前一個月則修正為增加 4.5%。國內訂單減少 2.9%，海外需求減少 4.2%，來自歐元區的訂單更大減 11.1%。訂單年增率仍為 1.6%，但 2–4 月合計較之前三個月減少 3.1%。

歐元區通膨達 3.2%，Isabel Schnabel 與 Yannis Stournaras 等官員認為，已不能單純忽略能源成本。企業計畫漲價、家庭通膨預期偏高，也加深央行疑慮。批評者則警告，不宜重蹈 2011 年升息、隨後因主權債務危機惡化而逆轉的覆轍，主張等待通膨持續性的證據，尤其美伊外交若有進展，能源衝擊可能減輕。

訂單疲弱有利於持有德債存續期間，但前端仍面對央行穩定通膨預期的決心。因此，一次預防性升息與連續升息之間的差別很重要：在疲弱景氣中持續緊縮，對曲線的風險不同於有限度回應能源價格。

南韓則同時受到成長、通膨與供給壓力影響。政府債券年內以本幣計價已虧損 7.5%，指標 3 年期殖利率升至約 3.9%，為 2023 年以來最高。AI 與半導體投資帶動央行將成長預測由 2.0% 上修至 2.6%，核心通膨達 2.5%，疲弱韓元又加重進口能源負擔。

交換市場反映至少三次升息，政策利率將由 2.5% 升至 3.25%。另一筆追加預算可能增加借款，但當局為抑制波動，已將 6 月計畫發債量較 5 月削減約 21%，主要集中於長天期。減量可帶來短期供給緩解，卻還無法化解成長轉強、通膨與匯率背後的賣壓。

日本投資人則為疲弱債市提供支撐。銀行信託帳戶常被視為退休基金的觀察指標，5 月淨買進海外債券 ¥3.16 兆，創現有統計紀錄。當月美國 10 年期殖利率一度達 4.69%，與日本同天期各自高點相比，約高出 200 個基點。這些買盤顯示，較高美債殖利率仍能吸引長期配置資金，即使日債殖利率上升、Fed 與中東局勢的不確定性，使配置時點更難掌握。

## 印尼融資計畫凸顯國家支持的界線

投資人質疑政府的干預政策，印尼本幣債與印尼盾持續承壓，匯率再創新低；主權美元債卻相對穩定。截至週五，一籃子政府債券相對美債利差約為 71 個基點，年內僅擴大 3 個基點。相較之下，亞洲高評等美元債利差已收窄 13 個基點，降至紀錄低點 50 個基點。

Danantara 計畫發行美元債，將檢驗這些外部買盤是否願意從直接主權債延伸至國家投資基金。除一般公司用途外，該基金向部分投資人表示，所得可能有一部分用來再融資今年稍早取得的 $10 億貸款。雖然它管理近 900 家國營企業，公開說明文件仍明列政府不保證這些票據。投資人需要衡量其戰略地位，以及債務契約實際提供的支持。

此外，Danantara 也規劃發行票息 3%、低於市場利率的本幣 Merah Putih 債券。美元借款可分散資金來源並延長天期，但也使幣別匹配與發行人信心更加重要。最終條件、定價讓利與訂單簿，將有助判斷市場如何評價沒有明確主權保證的國家相關借款人。

菲律賓監理機關關注的則是另一種風險集中。大型企業集團在 2027–2029 年將有約 1.6 兆披索、折合 $260 億債務到期，接近總債務的 25%；未來五年，美元債務平均占集團債務 37.6%。披索走弱增加本幣償債成本，燃料幾乎全靠進口，加上美債實質殖利率上升，又提高營運與再融資成本。

企業目前仍能透過債券、銀行貸款與內部資金滿足需求，金融穩定評估也認為銀行資本足以吸收非預期損失。不過，房地產估值偏高與無擔保消費信貸擴張，也被列為弱點。重點在企業到期日與幣別錯配，而非立即的主權融資危機；銀行資本則提供防止損失向外擴散的緩衝。

## 下一步看油價、通膨與標售

以色列與伊朗再度交火，使停火安排受到挑戰，WTI 上漲 0.84% 至 $91.30，布蘭特上漲 1.25% 至 $94.25。美元指數變動不大，下跌 0.02% 至 100.05，黃金下跌 0.03% 至 $4,335.90。美東時間下午 5 點過後，有條件降溫的消息為下一個交易日帶來緩解可能，但仍取決於停止攻擊的安排能否維持。

PIIE 的壓力情境估計，呈現高能源價格持續的代價。假設油價整年維持約 $120，加上 LNG、成品油與肥料成本上升，印度、越南與泰國產出相對基準情境約損失 3%，南韓 2.8%、中國 1.8%、美國 1.2%；中東與北非最大，至少 12%。這是附帶條件的估算，不是預測，假設油價也明顯高於週一收盤的 $90 多。

美國 CPI 將在 6 月 10 日美東時間 08:30 公布，PPI 在 6 月 11 日同一時間公布，FOMC 會議則在 6 月 16–17 日。整體 CPI 預期月增 0.5%、年增 4.2%，前值為 0.6% 與 3.8%；核心月增率預估由 0.4% 降至 0.2%。關鍵在於壓力是否仍集中於能源，或擴散至核心商品、服務與生產者利潤。基礎通膨放緩有利於前端延續反彈；若普遍偏強，則強化非農後的升息理由。

美債供給將在 6 月 9 日由國庫券轉向附息債，先標售 $580 億 3 年期，6 月 10 日增額發行 $390 億、票息 4.375% 的 10 年期，6 月 11 日再增額發行 $220 億、票息 5.000% 的 30 年期。三者合計 $1,190 億，均在 6 月 15 日交割。得標殖利率相對當時發行前交易的水準、投標人結構與交易商承接比重，將呈現最終投資人需求，通膨公布後尤其值得關注。若承接疲弱，供給可能加重長端持續落後的壓力。

德國 4 月工業生產將在 6 月 9 日公布，預估月增 0.5%，前值修正為下跌 0.1%。這份數據與 6 月 11 日 ECB 決策，將釐清訂單下滑是否反映至產出，以及政策如何因應。市場預期存款利率上調 25 個基點至 2.25%。若衝突持續降溫、產出疲弱，ECB 預告連續升息的理由會減少；若再度交火或指引偏鷹，石油進口經濟體與其債市仍將承壓。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有註明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為準。

overall_summary.headline: 家庭更擔憂就業與債務，前端美債收復部分跌幅
overall_summary.session_narrative:
紐約聯準銀行 5 月調查顯示，1 年期通膨預期降至 3.5%，求職展望轉弱，受訪者認為無法按時還款的風險也提高。2 年期美債殖利率扭轉亞洲升勢，收盤下跌 2 個基點至 4.15%；長端繼續走弱，10 年期升至 4.56%，30 年期達 5.03%。

反彈未延伸至實質利率：10 年期實質殖利率上升 2 個基點至 2.21%，損益兩平通膨率反而在油價上漲時降至 2.35%。半導體指數反彈 5.61%，高收益債 ETF 上漲，兩場國庫券標售吸收 $1,660.01 億供給，需求強弱不一。Blackstone、Cegid 與騰訊的潛在融資增加案源，哥倫比亞大學一份受到質疑的研究，則引發對非公開評等與保險業資本的關注。

ECB 決策前，德國訂單大幅下滑；南韓債券仍受到成長、通膨與財政壓力影響，日本退休基金相關帳戶創紀錄的海外買盤則提供支撐。接下來，美國通膨、$1,190 億附息債標售，以及中東降溫能否維持，將左右後續交易。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Front-End Treasuries Recover as Households Turn More Cautious

Short-dated Treasuries recovered some of Friday's payroll-driven losses on Monday as a New York Fed survey showed households becoming more worried about jobs and debt payments. The 2-year yield fell 2 basis points to 4.15%, reversing its earlier rise in Asian trading. Longer bonds continued to weaken: the 10-year yield added 1 basis point to 4.56% and the 30-year rose 2 to 5.03%.

The survey complicated, rather than overturned, the case for higher Fed rates. Near-term inflation expectations eased, job-finding prospects deteriorated and perceived payment risk rose. Yet intermediate and long real yields still increased, even as 10-year breakeven inflation slipped. Investors were willing to reverse part of the immediate front-end reaction to strong hiring, but not to lower the real return they required farther out the curve.

Technology shares also rebounded, led by semiconductors, and high-yield funds edged higher. Oil rose after renewed Israeli-Iranian strikes, leaving another uncertainty ahead of US inflation data and the ECB meeting. German factory orders weakened sharply, while Korea's semiconductor-led expansion and rising rate expectations continued to hurt local bonds. Against those competing pressures, Japanese pension-related accounts offered a substantial source of demand: their May purchases of overseas bonds reached a record.

## A Household Warning Tempers the Payroll Reaction

Treasuries initially extended Friday's losses in Asia, with 2- and 5-year yields rising more than longer maturities. Swaps again priced a quarter-point Fed increase by December and roughly a 16% chance of a second move. Renewed Middle East strikes added an oil-price risk to the strong employment data.

The New York Fed's May household survey was less reassuring about demand. Median 1-year inflation expectations fell to 3.5% from 3.6%, while 3- and 5-year expectations held at 3.1% and 3.0%. Respondents put the probability of losing a job at 15.1% and the chance of finding another after a loss at just 43.7%. The perceived probability of missing a minimum debt payment rose 1.2 percentage points to 12.6%, and expected spending growth slowed.

Those findings gave the front end some support after Friday's abrupt repricing. They pointed to greater household caution despite strong reported hiring, with slightly less near-term inflation anxiety. By the close, the 2-year had recovered and the 5-year yield was unchanged at 4.29%. The 2s10s spread widened 3 basis points to 41, while 2s30s widened 4 to 88.

The daily retracement was small beside the accumulated move. Over the week, 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields were still up 10, 11, 9 and 4 basis points; over the month, they had risen 25, 27, 18 and 8. The 2s5s10s butterfly increased 1 basis point to −13, showing modest 5-year underperformance against its wings on the day, while 2s10s30s rose 2 to −6.

Real yields continued to climb. The 5-year TIPS yield added 1 basis point to 1.82%, the 7-year rose 2 to 2.01%, and the 10-year gained 2 to 2.21%. The 20- and 30-year real yields increased 2 and 3 basis points to 2.57% and 2.77%. The 10-year breakeven fell 1 basis point to 2.35% despite higher crude prices. Energy remained a constraint on how readily the Fed could respond to weaker activity, but it was not lifting long-term inflation compensation at this close.

Cash markets remained calm. Coupon-equivalent bill yields were 3.68% at four weeks, unchanged; 3.67% at six weeks, down 1 basis point; and 3.69% at eight weeks, unchanged. The 13-, 17- and 26-week yields rose 3, 1 and 2 basis points to 3.74%, 3.76% and 3.82%, while the 52-week declined 3 to 3.82%.

The two completed bill auctions drew different levels of demand. Treasury accepted $89.001 billion of 91-day bills at a 3.640% high rate, with bid-to-cover improving to 2.79 from 2.69. Indirect bidders took 56.22%, direct bidders 5.87% and dealers 37.90%. The $77 billion 182-day sale cleared at 3.690%, with cover slipping to 2.75 from 2.84 and dealers taking 40.56%. Together, the sales absorbed $166.001 billion and settle June 11. Stronger 13-week cover and a higher dealer share in the longer sale left a mixed reception, without disruption in the shortest bills.

## New Financing Meets Questions About Private Ratings

Corporate risk appetite improved alongside equities. HYG gained 0.14% and JNK rose 0.07%, while the more rate-sensitive LQD fell 0.10% and EMB declined 0.13%. The S&P 500 added 0.30%, Nasdaq 100 rose 1.58% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 5.61%. VIX dropped 12.04% to 18.92, though the Nasdaq's weekly return remained negative after Friday's heavy losses.

The financing pipeline continued to expand. Blackstone was exploring a transaction exceeding $2 billion that would turn stakes in private investment funds into bonds, potentially one of the larger recent deals of its kind. Arcmont and Ares were leading a €1.1 billion loan for Silver Lake-backed software company Cegid. Both were still prospective transactions, with final terms and investor demand yet to be established.

A Columbia study released after the close raised a more fundamental question about privately rated debt. In a sample exceeding $4 trillion, such assets were about twice as likely to suffer a credit loss as publicly rated debt with the same grade. A private BBB rating carried impairment risk comparable to public BB+ or BB. US life insurers held about $481 billion of privately rated assets, representing 12% of rated credit portfolios, versus less than 2% in 2018. The researchers estimated that aligning ratings with observed performance could require roughly $4.5 billion of extra capital.

The findings came with important limits. The paper had not been peer-reviewed, loss rates were below 1% during the benign sample period, and Morningstar DBRS disputed both its methodology and conclusions. Even so, it put the treatment of private ratings and insurer capital requirements into focus as increasingly large financings move outside public markets.

Asian technology companies added both equity and debt to the prospective supply. Moonshot AI was seeking up to $2 billion of equity at a $30 billion valuation. Shortly after 5 p.m. New York time, Tencent was reported to be preparing roughly $3 billion of dual-currency bonds that could price as early as Tuesday. Equity can reduce the immediate need for borrowing, but the sector's expansion still requires substantial investment in chips, power and data centers. Tencent's final currency and maturity mix, pricing and allocation will provide a more concrete measure of debt-market demand than the announced target alone.

## Europe Weighs an Energy Response as Korean Bonds Slump

German factory orders exposed the weakness facing the ECB as it considered an increase in rates. April orders fell 3.8% from March, against an expected 1.2% decline, after the prior month was revised to a 4.5% gain. Domestic orders dropped 2.9%, foreign demand fell 4.2% and orders from the euro area plunged 11.1%. Orders were still up 1.6% from a year earlier, but the February–April period was 3.1% below the preceding three months.

With euro-area inflation at 3.2%, officials from Isabel Schnabel to Yannis Stournaras argued that energy costs could no longer simply be overlooked. Firms' plans to raise prices and elevated household inflation expectations added to their concern. Critics warned of repeating the ECB's 2011 increases, which were reversed as the sovereign-debt crisis deepened, and favored waiting for clearer evidence of persistence, especially if US-Iran diplomacy reduced the energy shock.

Weak orders support the case for holding Bund duration, but the front end remains exposed to a central bank intent on protecting inflation expectations. The distinction between one precautionary increase and a sequence is therefore important: further tightening into weak activity would pose a different risk to the curve from a limited response to energy prices.

Korea faced a more direct combination of growth, inflation and supply pressure. Government bonds had lost 7.5% in local-currency terms during the year, and the benchmark 3-year yield reached about 3.9%, its highest since 2023. AI and semiconductor investment helped lift the central bank's growth forecast to 2.6% from 2.0%, while core inflation reached 2.5%. A weak won added to the burden of imported energy.

Swaps priced at least three increases, taking the policy rate from 2.5% to 3.25%. Another supplementary budget could add borrowing, although authorities sought to contain volatility by cutting planned June bond sales about 21% from May, mainly at longer maturities. That reduction offers some near-term supply relief without resolving the stronger growth, inflation and currency pressures behind the selloff.

Japanese investors provided a counterweight to the weak bond-market tone. Bank trust accounts, often used as a proxy for pension funds, bought a net ¥3.16 trillion of overseas bonds in May, a record in the available series. US 10-year yields reached 4.69% during the month, roughly 200 basis points above comparable Japanese yields at their respective peaks. The purchases showed that higher Treasury yields could still draw structural demand, even as rising JGB yields and uncertainty over Fed policy and the Middle East complicated allocation decisions.

## Indonesia's Funding Plans Expose the Limits of State Support

Indonesian local bonds and the rupiah remained under pressure as investors questioned the government's interventionist agenda. The currency reached a record low, but sovereign dollar debt had been more stable: a government-bond basket traded about 71 basis points over Treasuries as of Friday, just 3 basis points wider for the year. High-grade Asian dollar spreads, by comparison, had tightened 13 basis points to a record 50.

Danantara's planned dollar issue will test how far that external demand extends beyond direct sovereign obligations. Alongside general corporate purposes, the state investment fund told some investors it could use part of the proceeds to refinance a $1 billion loan taken earlier in the year. Although it oversees nearly 900 state companies, the offering memorandum says the government will not guarantee the notes. Investors must therefore weigh the fund's strategic role against the actual contractual support for its debt.

The sale sits alongside proposed local-currency Merah Putih bonds carrying a below-market 3% coupon. Dollar borrowing could diversify funding and lengthen maturities, but it also increases the importance of currency matching and confidence in the issuer. Final terms, the pricing concession and the orderbook will help show how buyers value a state-linked borrower without an explicit sovereign guarantee.

Philippine regulators highlighted a different concentration of risk. Large conglomerates face about 1.6 trillion pesos, or $26 billion, of maturities in 2027–2029, nearly 25% of their debt. Dollar obligations average 37.6% of conglomerate debt over the next five years. Peso weakness increases the local-currency cost of those obligations, while near-total reliance on imported fuel and higher Treasury real yields add to operating and refinancing costs.

Companies had so far met their needs through bonds, bank loans and internal liquidity, and the financial-stability assessment found banks sufficiently capitalized to absorb unexpected losses. It also identified elevated property values and expanding unsecured consumer credit as vulnerabilities. The concern is a corporate maturity and currency mismatch, rather than an immediate sovereign funding problem, with bank capital providing a buffer against wider losses.

## Oil and Inflation Set the Next Tests

Renewed Israeli-Iranian strikes challenged the ceasefire and lifted WTI 0.84% to $91.30 and Brent 1.25% to $94.25. The dollar index was little changed, down 0.02% at 100.05, while gold slipped 0.03% to $4,335.90. Shortly after 5 p.m. ET, reports of conditional de-escalation introduced a new prospect of relief for the next session, dependent on whether the halt in strikes would hold.

A PIIE stress scenario illustrated the cost if high energy prices persisted. Holding oil near $120 for a full year, alongside higher LNG, refined-product and fertilizer costs, produced output losses relative to baseline of about 3% for India, Vietnam and Thailand, 2.8% for Korea, 1.8% for China and 1.2% for the US. The Middle East and North Africa had the largest modeled loss, at least 12%. These were conditional estimates, not forecasts, and assumed oil well above the low-to-mid $90s at Monday's close.

US CPI arrives at 08:30 ET on June 10, followed by PPI at the same time on June 11 and the FOMC meeting on June 16–17. Headline CPI is expected to rise 0.5% on the month and 4.2% on the year, after 0.6% and 3.8%, while core monthly inflation is forecast to slow to 0.2% from 0.4%. The key distinction is whether the pressure remains concentrated in energy or extends across core goods, services and producer margins. Softer underlying inflation would support the front-end recovery; broad strength would reinforce the post-payroll case for higher rates.

The Treasury calendar moves from bills to coupons on June 9 with $58 billion of 3-year notes, followed by a $39 billion 10-year reopening on June 10 at a 4.375% coupon and a $22 billion 30-year reopening on June 11 at 5.000%. All three settle June 15, for $119 billion gross. Auction yields against prevailing when-issued levels, bidder composition and dealer takedown will show whether end-user demand is sufficient, especially after the inflation release. A weak reception could add supply pressure to the long end's continuing underperformance.

Germany's April industrial production on June 9 is expected to rise 0.5% after a revised 0.1% decline. That release and the ECB decision on June 11 will help establish whether the order slump translates into weaker output and how policymakers respond. Consensus expects a 25-basis-point increase in the deposit rate to 2.25%. Durable de-escalation and weak production would give the ECB less reason to signal repeated increases; renewed attacks or hawkish guidance would keep oil-importing economies and their bond markets under pressure.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
The New York Fed's May survey showed 1-year inflation expectations easing to 3.5%, weaker job-finding prospects and a higher perceived risk of missing debt payments. The 2-year Treasury yield reversed its Asian rise and closed 2 basis points lower at 4.15%. Longer bonds weakened, with the 10-year at 4.56% and the 30-year at 5.03%.

The recovery did not extend to real yields: the 10-year rose 2 basis points to 2.21%, while breakeven inflation slipped to 2.35% despite firmer oil. Semiconductor shares rebounded 5.61%, high-yield funds gained and two bill auctions absorbed $166.001 billion with mixed demand. Prospective Blackstone, Cegid and Tencent financings added to the pipeline, while a disputed Columbia study raised questions about private ratings and insurer capital.

German orders fell sharply ahead of the ECB decision, whereas Korea's growth, inflation and fiscal pressures continued to hurt bonds. Record Japanese pension-related overseas purchases offered a source of demand. US inflation, $119 billion of coupon auctions and whether Middle East de-escalation holds now shape the next sessions.
